chunks: Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said:

I asked Aba al-Hasan, peace be upon him, and said: "May I be your ransom, I purchased a piece of land next to mine for one thousand dirhams. When I gathered the money, I was informed that the land was a waqf."
So he said: "The purchase of waqf property is not permissible, and do not mix its yield with your wealth. Give it to those for whom it was endowed."
I said: "I do not know any rightful owner for it." He said: "Give its yield in charity."

key_terms.الْغَلَّةَ: The yield, produce, or income generated from the land.
key_terms.تَصَدَّقْ: Give in charity when the rightful beneficiaries cannot be identified.
key_terms.شِرَاءُ: The act of purchase or buying, here referring to an invalid transaction involving waqf.
key_terms.مَالِكَ: Your personal wealth or property, with which the waqf yield must not be mixed.
key_terms.وَقْفٌ: An endowed property dedicated for a specified religious or charitable purpose.

ai.seo_question: What should be done if someone discovers that purchased land is actually waqf property?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the sale of waqf property is not permissible and that its produce must not be absorbed into one's personal wealth. If the designated beneficiaries of the waqf are unknown, its yield should be given in charity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5576 - Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (as), peace be upon him, and said: "May I be your ransom, I purchased a piece of land next to mine for one thousand dirhams. When I gathered the money, I was informed that the land was an endowment (waqf)."
Imam (as) replied: "The purchase of endowment property is not permissible, and do not mix its yield with your wealth. Instead, give its yield to those for whom it was endowed."

I said: "I do not know who its rightful beneficiaries are."
Imam (as) said: "Then give its yield in charity."
